dominance_intro.objective: Can two dark-furred dogs produce a light-furred puppy? Cross two Bb parents and explain why.
dominance_intro.question: What percentage of puppies will have dark fur? What percentage will have light fur?
dominance_intro.lesson: A dominant allele affects the phenotype in a heterozygote. Dominant does not mean stronger or more common.

dominance_revisit.objective: Test whether an Ee upright-eared dog crossed with an ee floppy-eared dog can have floppy-eared offspring.
dominance_revisit.question: Predict the percentage with upright ears and with floppy ears.
dominance_revisit.lesson: An Ee dog looks upright-eared in this teaching model, but can still pass on e. Follow the alleles, not just appearance.

hidden_genotypes.objective: Cross a dark Bb dog and a light bb dog. Can puppies with different appearances share an allele?
hidden_genotypes.question: Predict the percentage of dark-furred and light-furred puppies.
hidden_genotypes.lesson: Genotype names the allele pair; phenotype names the observable trait. A Bb dog is dark, yet can pass on b.

punnett_grid.objective: Cross two Tt dogs. Use the four combinations of gametes to predict long and short tails.
punnett_grid.question: How many of the four equally likely combinations make a short tail?
punnett_grid.lesson: A Punnett square enumerates equally likely allele combinations; it predicts probabilities, not the outcome of a single birth.

variation.objective: Cross an amber-eyed Cc dog with a blue-eyed cc dog. Explore how existing alleles produce variation among offspring.
variation.question: Predict the fraction of amber-eyed and blue-eyed puppies.
variation.lesson: Sexual inheritance reshuffles existing alleles. This variation is not a mutation caused by the puppies needing to change.

coat_inheritance.objective: Apply the allele model to a second characteristic. Cross Ll and Ll to investigate coat length.
coat_inheritance.question: What proportion of puppies should have short coats?
coat_inheritance.lesson: The same inheritance rule can model several separate traits. Actual dog coat length is more complex than this fictional single-gene exercise.
